title: Claims Payment Computation Note — RideLink Mileage Amount
content:
This note sets out how the amount of a Non-Emergency Medical Transportation mileage entry is computed for a trip on RideLink Mileage Reimbursement.

**The trip.** The trip is the one on the member's latest registered outbound leg, identified by its reservation number; its registered legs are the legs that carry that reservation number.

**Formal clause.** The approved miles are the round trip: the registered one-way miles of the trip's outbound and return legs added together, each measured by the shortest driving route. Every approved mile is paid at the level's standard mileage rate, and the amount is rounded to the nearest cent once, on the final amount only.

The standard mileage rate is the per-mile figure listed in the level's mileage reimbursement terms.

## Input — computation — output

| Step | Computation |
|---|---|
| Approved miles | Outbound leg's registered one-way miles plus return leg's registered one-way miles |
| Amount before rounding | Approved miles times the level's standard mileage rate |
| Amount | Rounded to the nearest cent, once |

## Worked example

*Hypothetical inputs:* outbound leg registered at 62.4 one-way miles, return leg at 62.4 one-way miles, on a level rate of 0.21 USD a mile.

1. Approved miles: 62.4 plus 62.4 is 124.8 miles.
2. Amount before rounding: 124.8 times 0.21 is 26.208 USD.
3. Amount: 26.21 USD.

*A second hypothetical:* legs of 18.0 and 22.5 one-way miles give 40.5 approved miles; at 0.21 USD a mile that is 8.505, rounded once to 8.51 USD.
